name: Vietnamese quan họ Bắc Ninh
lineage: Vietnamese quan họ Bắc Ninh antiphonal courtship-song tradition of the Bắc Ninh province, the Red River Delta region north of Hanoi. Performance involves paired female-and-male choral groups (liền chị women, liền anh men) from neighboring villages who exchange improvised verse-and-response over the course of a year of festival visits, with the courtship-exchange the formal narrative-arc of the repertoire. Vocal style features unaccompanied (originally — modern stage performance often adds chamber-ensemble accompaniment) two-or-three-voice female and male chorus in heterophonic-melodic-elaboration register, with characteristic Vietnamese pentatonic-modal vocabulary and the distinctive vibrato-ornament called nẩy hột ("rice-grain vibrato," a precisely-articulated rapid pitch-and-amplitude wobble unique to quan họ vocal-aesthetic). Verse-forms draw on canonical four-line, six-eight-line, and seven-seven-six-eight Vietnamese poetic-meter structures. The forty-nine documented "kết-chạ" (sworn-sister-village) pair-relationships constitute the social-structural infrastructure of the tradition. Documentation records two hundred and forty-nine quan họ villages across the region. Distinguished from ca trù by quan họ's village-festival-collective (vs chamber-literary) functional context; distinguished from xoan (the adjacent ritual-village tradition) by quan họ's courtship-exchange (vs ancestor-veneration) functional framing; distinguished from southern Vietnamese đờn ca tài tử by northern Red-River-Delta dialect-specific cadential conventions.
